Each session features a different theme and fun challenges to keep students motivated and actively involved.

rows: Follow coach commands, range boundaries, and safe arrow-retrieval procedures.

items: Archery is conducted only in a designated area that has been inspected and approved by the school.
The coach establishes and controls the shooting line, waiting line, target area, and safe retrieval procedure.
Students must never point a bow at another person, even when no arrow is nocked.
No student may nock or release an arrow until the coach gives explicit permission.
All shooting must be directed toward approved targets with suitable backstop and overshoot containment.
Students remain behind the waiting line until the coach gives the signal to approach targets.
Arrows are retrieved only after all bows are down, the range is declared clear, and the coach gives permission.
Equipment is inspected before each session; damaged bows, arrows, strings, or protective gear are removed from use.
The number of active shooters and the coach-to-student ratio must be appropriate to the facility, age group, equipment, and school policy.
Flip-flop targets must be locked and stationary before shooting; target changes occur only while the range is closed.

Spinning and moving target activities require purpose-built equipment, a documented risk assessment, school approval, and qualified instructor control. A static or non-shooting alternative is used if any control is unavailable.

Trickshoot activities must not involve people in the arrow path, human-held targets, blindfold shooting, shooting over people, or hazardous props. Advanced demonstrations are instructor-only and separately risk-assessed.
The coach stops activity immediately if an unsafe condition, equipment fault, or unauthorised person enters the controlled area.

Instruction is progressive and adapted to each student’s age, readiness, and demonstrated swimming ability.

blocks.text: Roundnet is a team sport played around a low, circular net placed close to the ground. Two teams of two players take turns hitting a ball onto the net so that it rebounds toward the opposing team and becomes difficult to return. This program introduces students to the fundamental skills and rules of Roundnet, progressing toward 2 vs 2 match play through active, enjoyable, and age-appropriate learning activities.

blocks.text: Flag Football is a non-tackling version of American Football. blocks.text: Mozaiq Magic Academy is an engaging extracurricular program that introduces students to the art of magic, illusion, and performance. Through age-appropriate activities using cards, coins, cups, ropes, silks, and other simple props, students learn how to create entertaining effects while developing confidence, creativity, communication, and critical thinking.

The program is designed as a practical, highly interactive learning experience. Each session combines a concise theory and instructor-demonstration block with guided practice, challenges, and performance games. The emphasis is on safe entertainment, respectful audience interaction, and responsible use of magic techniques.

items: Only instructor-approved, age-appropriate props may be used.

Magic is presented as entertainment and illusion; students must not claim supernatural powers or use tricks to deceive, intimidate, or embarrass others.
Props must be counted, checked, and returned safely at the end of each session.

blocks.text: Students are assessed through observation, practice tasks, peer interaction, and the final performance. Assessment should recognize progress, effort, safe practice, and confidence—not only technical perfection.

blocks.text: Ultimate Frisbee is a non-contact team sport played with a flying disc. Teams advance the disc by passing to teammates and score by completing a catch in the opposing end zone. The sport develops throwing and catching skills, agility, spatial awareness, communication, decision-making, and teamwork. Its distinctive Spirit of the Game principle encourages honesty, mutual respect, self-officiation, and fair play.

This 10-session curriculum is designed for school-age learners and progresses from introductory skills to tactical understanding and modified match play. Activities are adapted to student age, ability, group size, weather, and the available SIS playing area.

items: Perform introductory backhand and forehand throws with improved control.
Catch a flying disc safely and consistently at an age-appropriate level.
Use a pivot and move into open space to support teammates.
Apply simple offensive and defensive principles in small-sided games.
Understand basic scoring, turnovers, and key rules of modified Ultimate Frisbee.
Participate positively in team play and demonstrate the Spirit of the Game.

blocks.text: Focus: Discovering the sport, equipment, basic rules, and Spirit of the Game.
Session objective: Students become familiar with the flying disc, safe handling, basic passing, and cooperative play.

rows: Warm-up: light jogging, dynamic stretches, shoulder and wrist mobility.
Introduction: what Ultimate Frisbee is, field zones, basic objective, non-contact principle, and Spirit of the Game.
Disc familiarisation: grip, stance, release direction, and coach demonstration of a basic backhand.
Partner practice: short-distance underhand-free backhand introduction and safe disc retrieval.
Game 1 – Keep the Disc: small groups complete consecutive passes without a defender.
Game 2 – 3v3 Passing Challenge: teams score a point for completing a set number of passes.
Team challenge: move the disc from a start line to a target zone using passes only.
Cool-down and reflection: one rule and one skill learned today.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Identify the disc and basic playing objective.
Demonstrate a basic ready position and introductory backhand grip.
Show cooperation and safe behaviour during group activities.

blocks.text: Focus: Backhand and forehand throwing mechanics, accuracy, and controlled release.
Session objective: Students practise the two foundational throws and select a suitable throw for a short passing task.

rows: Warm-up: dynamic movement, arm circles, wrist mobility, and partner coordination.
Theory and demonstration: backhand grip, stance, weight transfer, release point, and follow-through.
Backhand practice: partner throws at short distance; focus on flat release and controlled power.
Forehand explanation: grip, side-on stance, wrist action, and safe short-distance release.
Forehand introduction: close-range partner attempts with coach feedback.
Accuracy Throwing Challenge: aim at marked gates or cone targets.
Moving Target Passing: receiver moves between cones while the passer leads the target.
Team Passing Competition: teams earn points for accurate completed passes.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Demonstrate introductory backhand and forehand mechanics.
Adjust throwing force and direction for a partner.
Understand that accuracy and control are more important than maximum power.

blocks.text: Focus: Two-hand catching, tracking the disc, and receiving while moving.
Session objective: Students improve confidence and control when receiving passes from different directions and at manageable speeds.

rows: Warm-up: jogging, hand-eye coordination, and gentle partner tosses.
Theory: tracking the disc, safe catching position, two-hand/pancake catch, and when to use a one-hand catch.
Stationary catching: partner throws at chest and waist height; receiver secures the disc with two hands.
Moving catching: short routes forward and sideways; passer leads the receiver.
Catching Relay: teams complete a sequence of catches and returns.
Catch and Move Game: players receive, establish control, and pass to the next teammate.
Team Catching Competition: score for clean catches in marked zones.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Track the flight of the disc and prepare hands early.
Use a controlled two-hand catch where appropriate.
Receive a pass while moving at a safe speed.

blocks.text: Focus: Pivot foot, balance, legal movement, and passing from a stationary position.
Session objective: Students learn to establish a pivot and create passing options without travelling.

rows: Warm-up: agility steps, balance holds, and controlled direction changes.
Theory: establishing a pivot foot, legal pivot movement, travelling, and balance.
Pivot practice: hold the disc, keep one pivot foot grounded, and rotate under control.
Pivot and pass: partner offers targets on both sides; passer pivots before releasing.
Cone Movement Challenge: move to a cone, stop under control, pivot, and pass.
Pivot and Pass Game: small groups complete passes while staying within the pivot rule.
3v3 Keep Possession: defenders apply light, non-contact pressure.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Establish and maintain a pivot foot.
Pivot with balance and awareness of nearby players.
Avoid travelling while preparing a pass.

blocks.text: Focus: Cutting, leading passes, spacing, and moving without the disc.
Session objective: Students learn to create passing options by changing speed and direction and communicating with teammates.

rows: Warm-up: jogging, acceleration/deceleration, and change-of-direction movement.
Theory: cutting, leading a receiver, clearing space, spacing, and give-and-go movement.
Basic cutting drill: run to a cone, change direction, and receive a leading pass.
Give-and-go drill: pass, move into open space, and receive a return pass.
Find the Open Space Challenge: players move to unoccupied gates to receive.
3v3 Attacking Game: teams aim to complete passes while maintaining spacing.
Team-to-End-Zone Challenge: create a sequence of cuts and complete a catch in the target zone.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Move into open space to support the player with the disc.
Use a simple cut and give-and-go combination.
Communicate and avoid crowding teammates.

blocks.text: Focus: Defensive stance, marking distance, shadowing, and safe interception opportunities.
Session objective: Students practise non-contact defence and understand how to limit passing options without physical contact.

rows: Warm-up: lateral shuffles, reaction steps, and controlled acceleration.
Theory: marking position, legal defensive distance, body control, and non-contact rules.
Shadow marking: defender mirrors the thrower’s movement without contact.
Passing-lane drill: defenders read the space and position themselves to discourage a pass.
Defensive Reaction Challenge: react to a change of direction while keeping safe distance.
1v1 Channel Game: attacker attempts to reach a target gate; defender shadows without contact.
3v3 Attack vs Defence: apply marking and passing-lane awareness.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Adopt a balanced defensive stance.
Shadow an opponent while maintaining safe non-contact distance.
Recognise passing lanes and defend responsibly.

blocks.text: Focus: Triangle passing, support angles, possession, and decision-making.
Session objective: Students combine throwing, catching, movement, and communication to maintain possession under light pressure.

rows: Warm-up: partner passing while moving and dynamic mobility.
Theory: support angles, triangle formation, resetting possession, and communication cues.
Triangle passing: three players maintain passing angles and move after each pass.
Give-and-go combination: pass, cut, receive, and reset.
Passing Under Pressure: small groups complete passes while defenders occupy lanes.
4v4 Possession Game: maintain possession with a pass-count target.
End-Zone Attack Challenge: teams use width and support to create a scoring opportunity.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Create useful support angles for the thrower.
Use basic team communication and movement patterns.
Make simple decisions to retain possession.

blocks.text: Focus: End-zone scoring, turnovers, stall count introduction, and transitions.
Session objective: Students understand how to score and how possession changes during a modified game.

rows: Theory: scoring in the end zone, turnovers, restart/check procedures, and introductory stall count.
End-zone passing drill: complete a controlled pass to a teammate in the scoring area.
Transition drill: switch from attack to defence after a dropped or intercepted pass.
Scoring Accuracy Challenge: pass to moving receivers entering a marked end zone.
4v4 End-Zone Game: apply scoring and turnover rules.
Match Scenario Challenge: restart play and respond to a change of possession.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Identify the end zone and explain how a point is scored.
Recognise common turnovers and basic restarts.
Apply the rules in a modified game.

blocks.text: Focus: Team roles, tactical application, communication, and modified tournament play.
Session objective: Students apply the skills and rules learned in previous sessions in short, small-sided matches.

rows: Warm-up: team movement and progressive passing.
Review: key rules, Spirit of the Game, team roles, and simple match strategy.
Passing accuracy refresher: backhand, forehand, and catching in pairs.
Tactical movement drill: cutting, spacing, and defensive positioning.
Team formation and strategy: assign roles and agree on communication cues.
Mini Match – Round 1: modified 3v3, 4v4, or 5v5 depending on numbers and space.
Mini Match – Round 2: rotate teams or roles and apply one tactical improvement.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Apply core throwing, catching, movement, and defensive skills in a game.
Understand basic team roles and match flow.
Demonstrate fair play and positive communication.

blocks.text: Focus: Skills review, performance assessment, final modified match, and reflection.
Session objective: Students demonstrate their progress and reflect on personal and team development over the 10 sessions.

rows: Warm-up: student-led dynamic warm-up with coach supervision.
Review: key rules, Spirit of the Game, and final match expectations.
Throwing and catching assessment: short passing accuracy and secure catches.
Movement and teamwork assessment: pivot, cut, support, and communication.
Final team preparation: agree on tactics, positions, and fair-play commitments.
Final Match – Round 1: modified small-sided match.
Final Match – Round 2: rotate roles and complete the final game.

blocks.text: Expected learning outcomes

items: Demonstrate progress in fundamental disc skills.
Participate in a modified match and apply basic rules.
Reflect on teamwork, sportsmanship, and personal improvement.

Empowering Students Through Sports, Skills & Character Development

blocks.text: Floorball is a fast-paced indoor team sport played with lightweight sticks and a lightweight plastic ball with holes. Players work together to move the ball, create scoring opportunities, and score in the opposing goal. The program introduces students to the sport through progressive skill development, teamwork, movement, tactical awareness, and supervised small-sided games.

rows: Mozaiq Floorball Academy – After School Activity (ASA)
50% Technical Drilling & Theory + 50% Games & Practical Application

blocks.text: Each session is structured to balance focused skill instruction with active play.

rows: Technical Drilling & Theory – warm-up, demonstration, skill practice and tactical explanation
Games & Practical Application – challenges, small-sided games, team competitions and skill application

blocks.text: Note: The 27/28-minute split is the practical allocation of the requested 50/50 format within a 55-minute session.

rows: Identify basic floorball equipment, playing-area features and key rules.
Demonstrate safe stick grip, ready position, dribbling and ball handling.
Execute a basic push pass and receive a moving ball with control.
Demonstrate basic push-shot or wrist-shot technique toward a target.
Move into space and support teammates during attacking play.
Use basic defensive positioning and attempt safe interceptions.
Participate in small-sided floorball games and apply learned skills.
Show discipline, respect, inclusion and fair play.
One per student; provide suitable lengths for participants.
10–15 balls, or enough to maintain active participation.
2 units; portable goals are suitable where permitted.
20–30 units for lanes, targets and boundaries.
1 set, optional for introductory sessions; required for formal goalkeeper practice.
1 accessible kit; confirm school emergency procedures.

blocks.text: Quantities should be adjusted to the final participant count, court layout and equipment available at SIS.

items: Students must wear appropriate sportswear and non-marking indoor sports shoes suitable for the playing surface.
Conduct a dynamic warm-up before technical drills and games.
Keep the stick blade low and under control; no high or uncontrolled stick swings.
No intentional body checking, pushing, tripping or other unsafe physical contact.
Do not strike an opponent’s body or stick. Use controlled stick movements and maintain personal space.
During shooting drills, students must shoot only when the lane is clear and must wait behind the designated line.
Use only suitable floorball balls and inspect sticks, goals and playing surfaces before each session.
Stop immediately when the coach or supervising staff blows the whistle.
Use suitable protective equipment for goalkeeper activities; do not conduct goalkeeper drills without appropriate supervision and equipment.
The coach must supervise all activities, adapt drills to students’ age and ability, and follow SIS safeguarding and emergency procedures.
Students should report pain, injury, dizziness or feeling unwell to the coach immediately.
Learning by Playing: Introduce skills through purposeful, enjoyable activities.
Progressive Skill Development: Move from simple individual tasks to partner, group and game situations.
Small-Sided Games: Use 1-vs-1, 2-vs-2, 3-vs-3 and 4-vs-4 formats to increase touches and participation.
Team Challenges: Use friendly competitions to build motivation and positive team spirit.
Practical Demonstrations: Coaches demonstrate each technique and explain key safety points before practice.
Positive Coaching: Encourage effort, confidence, creativity, inclusion and respect.

blocks.text: Students are assessed formatively throughout the program. The final session includes a practical review of individual skills and game participation.

items: Understand the fundamental concepts, equipment and rules of floorball.

Demonstrate teamwork, communication, discipline and fair play.
